answer: Anchor every identity to one postal address proven by mail. The network sends a one-time code to that address, the agent enters it in fourteen days, and one address backs a single identity per year. Returned mail revokes it at once, and peers spot-check a random sample each epoch. Faking ten thousand agents means renting ten thousand real mailboxes at $120 a year, $1.2 million annually, plus 20,000 hours collecting codes. A marble copy looks fine in plaster, but the kernel stays stone: like a mesa carved from one rock, an identity tied to one mailbox cannot be split into copies.
